points.description: Says a stack is a data structure (or a structure/collection used for storing data) that can hold/store elements or items. Equivalent wording such as 'a container for data' earns the marks. A bare 'list of items' with no idea of a structure for storing data earns partial credit only.
points.partial_credit: Half marks for describing a stack only as a collection/list of items without identifying it as a data structure or storage structure.

levels.says: Describes a stack only as a collection or list of items, without saying it is a data structure or a structure for storing data.

points.description: States the last-in-first-out (LIFO) property: the last/most recently added item is the first to be removed, or equivalently the first item added is removed last, or removal is in reverse order of addition. Simply saying 'LIFO' earns full marks. A vague statement that order matters but not which item comes out first earns partial credit.
points.partial_credit: Half marks for mentioning a special/reverse removal order without making clear that the most recently added item is removed first.

levels.says: Mentions that items are removed in a special or reverse order, but does not state that the most recently added item is removed first or otherwise make the LIFO order clear.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both ideas: a stack is a data structure/collection for storing elements, and it has the LIFO property. Part marks are available when one idea is vague or only partly stated. No marks are earned for an answer that gives neither storage nor LIFO order.
